questions.scenario: A company must choose between RAG and fine-tuning for a support assistant. Product documentation changes weekly, and answers must reference specific documents. Which is correct and why?
options: RAG, because it retrieves current documents at query time and enables citation
Fine-tuning, because it is cheaper than RAG
questions.explain: Weekly changes plus a citation requirement both point to RAG, which reads live documents and can reference them. Fine-tuning is more expensive than RAG, cannot cite sources, and guarantees nothing.

questions.scenario: Which of these would MOST directly reduce the per-request cost of a high-volume GenAI application?
options: Shortening prompts and capping output tokens
questions.explain: Cost is driven by tokens in and out, so shorter prompts and capped outputs reduce it directly. More examples and a bigger context window both increase token usage.

questions.scenario: Which statement about labelled and unlabelled data is correct?
options: Supervised learning requires labelled data; unsupervised learning works with unlabelled data
Labels are only needed for image data
questions.explain: Labels are the dividing line: supervised learning learns from labelled examples, unsupervised learning finds structure without them. Labelling is often the most expensive part of an ML project.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service would convert a customer service call recording into searchable text?
questions.explain: Transcribe converts speech to text, which can then be searched or analysed. Polly generates speech, Kendra searches existing documents, and Personalize makes recommendations.

questions.scenario: Which describes the main advantage of using a managed AI service such as Amazon Comprehend over building a custom model?
options: Faster delivery with no ML expertise required
It always produces more accurate results than any custom model
It removes the need for data governance
questions.explain: Managed services deliver quickly without ML expertise. A custom model can outperform them for specialised tasks, governance still applies, and usage is billed.

questions.scenario: What does the term 'nondeterministic' mean when applied to generative AI?
options: The same input may produce different outputs on different runs
questions.explain: Nondeterminism means repeated identical prompts can yield different responses, which complicates testing and reproducibility. Lowering temperature reduces but does not eliminate it.

questions.scenario: Which is the MOST appropriate first step when a GenAI application is found to produce occasional toxic language?
options: Configure Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to filter harmful content
Retrain the foundation model from scratch
questions.explain: Guardrails filters harmful content and is the direct, proportionate control. Retraining a foundation model is wildly disproportionate, higher temperature worsens it, and removing logging hides the problem.

questions.scenario: Which is a valid reason to prefer a more interpretable model over a more accurate but opaque one?
options: Regulatory requirements demand explanations for individual decisions
Opaque models cannot be deployed on AWS
questions.explain: In regulated domains such as lending and healthcare, the ability to explain individual decisions can outweigh a marginal accuracy gain. This is the safety-versus-transparency trade-off the exam guide names.

questions.scenario: Which service provides evidence collection to support audits of AI workloads?
questions.explain: Audit Manager continuously collects evidence to support audits. AWS Artifact provides AWS's own compliance reports, while Polly, Forecast and Lex are AI capabilities.

questions.scenario: Which practice provides an audit trail of every interaction with a foundation model?
options: Enabling logging of model invocations and API activity
questions.explain: Logging model invocations and API activity creates the audit trail governance requires. Disabling CloudTrail and using the root user are both explicitly discouraged.

questions.scenario: Which term describes providing exactly one example in the prompt?
questions.explain: One-shot supplies a single example, zero-shot none, and few-shot several. Chain-of-thought is about step-by-step reasoning rather than the number of examples.

questions.scenario: A company wants to measure whether its GenAI assistant is meeting business objectives. Which metric is MOST relevant?
options: Cost per interaction and task completion rate
Number of tokens in the vocabulary
questions.explain: Business alignment is measured by outcomes such as cost per interaction, task completion rate and user satisfaction. GPU utilisation, vocabulary size and file size are technical details.

questions.scenario: Which describes a diffusion model?
options: A model type commonly used to generate images
questions.explain: Diffusion models generate images, whereas transformer-based LLMs generate text. Both are foundation model families named in the exam guide.

questions.scenario: Which service should be used when a company wants full control to build, train and deploy a custom ML model?
questions.explain: SageMaker AI is the platform for building, training and deploying custom models with full control. Bedrock provides access to existing foundation models, and Comprehend and Polly are pre-built capabilities.

questions.scenario: Which describes the effect of high variance in a machine learning model?
options: The model fits training data closely but generalises poorly to new data
The model ignores the training data entirely
questions.explain: High variance corresponds to overfitting: excellent on training data, poor on unseen data. High bias corresponds to underfitting, where the model learns too little.

questions.scenario: Which TWO approaches help verify that a GenAI system's answers are grounded in real source material?
options: Retrieving and citing source documents through RAG
Applying confidence scoring and output validation
questions.explain: Grounding is verified by retrieving and citing real sources and by validating output with confidence scoring. Token limits and temperature do not establish grounding, and removing human review weakens assurance.

questions.scenario: Which best explains why prompt engineering is usually attempted before fine-tuning?
options: It is far cheaper and faster, and often sufficient
It always produces better results than fine-tuning
Fine-tuning is not available on AWS
Prompt engineering permanently changes the model
questions.explain: Prompt engineering costs nothing beyond tokens and is often enough, which is why it comes first in the cost order. It does not always outperform fine-tuning, and it never changes the model itself.

questions.scenario: Which describes an appropriate use of Amazon Bedrock Guardrails in a regulated industry?
options: Blocking prohibited topics and masking personal data in responses
questions.explain: Guardrails blocks denied topics, filters harmful content and masks PII — directly useful under regulation. It does not train models or manage infrastructure.

questions.scenario: Which stage of the AI/ML lifecycle involves checking model quality against held-out data before release?
questions.explain: Evaluation tests the trained model against held-out data before release. Deployment follows it, and monitoring watches the model once it is live.

questions.scenario: A company deploys an AI system that affects access to financial services. Which responsible AI practice is MOST important?
options: Assessing fairness across demographic groups and enabling explanation of decisions
Maximising response speed above all else
Removing human oversight to reduce cost
questions.explain: High-stakes decisions demand fairness assessment and explainability, supported by Clarify, Model Cards and human review. Speed, reduced documentation and removed oversight all increase risk in this setting.
